tb21_profile.skill: Git object-store forensics: find data that survives a history rewrite as an unreachable object, then actually expunge it (rewrite, expire reflogs, prune packs) without disturbing anything else
tb21_profile.domain: Git internals - objects, packfiles, refs, reflog, fsck, filter-branch/filter-repo - and secret leakage
tb21_profile.task_form: recover-hidden-data plus surgical repair, verified both ways: secret found AND secret absent everywhere

verifier_notes: No grade overturned. Two of the very closest candidates are FREE and therefore excluded from final_top10: tw_6480 (recover a dangling blob from the object store - the exact recovery step) and security_20260606_153537_001 (secrets after git reset --hard HEAD~1). security_20260509_154924_007 and security_20260419_182351_003 are also FREE audits of the same scenario. Note that for this TB2.1 task a FREE verifier is especially dangerous: a file containing a plausible secret[...] string passes a substring check without the repo ever being cleaned.
searches: tools.py search rebench '(?i)git-machete|dulwich|GitPython|pre-commit|detect-secrets|gitlint|nbdime|dvc exp|git ls-files|\.git/|git blame|git stash|git rev-parse'

TMax-15K.reason: Search a repo's git history for an API key committed then removed - the recovery half verbatim, strong verifier.
Find a fallback API key that was committed and later removed from history; identical forensics, bundled with a binary-inspection subtask.
Inspect history of a local repo to recover a key hardcoded in an earlier commit and save the exact string - same deliverable shape.
A secret committed in the same commit as a bug and removed later; requires diffing history rather than reading the working tree.
Recover an API key and pin the exact commit that introduced it - commit-level attribution on top of secret recovery.
Identify the bad commit hash and fix on top without rewriting main; teaches when history rewriting is and is not allowed.
3am repair of a broken pipeline repo; git is the workspace rather than the subject, so only incident-triage habits transfer.
Recover a lost test asset out of the repository's history while also fixing the build - retrieving deleted content from git.
Walk a git history to locate the regression commit; history navigation only, nothing about the object store.
Debug an intermittently failing CI pipeline on master; repository context but no forensics or rewriting.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Locate the dangling commit that added secret.key in a bare repo and git show it - exactly the unreachable-object hunt this task needs.
Use the reflog to prove the secret.key commit was reset away and record its hash; reflog forensics on a removed secret.
Capture the full diff of the secret.key commit before rewriting history away - recover first, then purge, in that order.
Expunge the commit that added secret.key from remote history and produce the forensic deliverables; the cleanup half.
Remove a mistakenly committed secret.key from a remote and force-push the corrected history, with forensic reports.
Repair a broken repository until git fsck --full reports no errors and no dangling objects - the state the cleanup must reach.
Pack the object store and report on dangling objects from a full fsck; teaches how gc and packing hide or expose objects.
Find the pre-rebase tip using only the reflog, no guessing - reading history that the visible branch no longer shows.
Document the pre-rebase baseline from the reflog and diff against it; same reasoning about what a rewrite discarded.
Enumerate every object in the store into a manifest after an fsck; object-store literacy but no recovery.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Recover the content of a dangling blob that was staged but never committed - the precise recovery step here. FREE verifier, so excluded from top10.
Remove the commit that added secret.key from a remote's history; the purge half, with a graded verifier.
A secret deleted during a Docker build is still recoverable from an earlier layer - same deleted-but-retained-by-the-store principle.
Nuclear reset of a messy repo: back up the tree, re-create the repository clean; strong verifier, adjacent to purging history.
Install a gitleaks pre-commit hook and prove it blocks a secret; the detection side of leaked-credential handling.
Extract one subtree's history into a standalone repository - a real filtering rewrite that must preserve unrelated commits.
Build a commit with plumbing only (hash-object, write-tree, commit-tree); object-model fluency you need to read a dangling object.
Manage an encrypted secret with git-secret; secrets-in-repos domain, no forensics.
Remove a stale worktree and prune its references so the repo is clean; pruning references is part of a real purge.
Use git bisect to find an injected bad commit; history navigation, but nothing removed or recovered.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: Git config is not carried into temporary-directory experiments; debugging how a tool drives a real repository underneath.
DVCFileSystem breaks when the repo has no SCM; reasoning about repository state a tool assumes but may not have.
dvc exp remove --queue -A returns incomplete results; enumerating refs that should all have been removed - an incomplete-purge bug.
Repository cloning silently does nothing; a git operation that appears to succeed while leaving the store untouched.
Repository abbreviation expansion broken; parsing how repositories are addressed, shallow transfer.
Repository objects fail to initialise from their on-disk JSON; managing checked-out repos as data.
Repo and module names swapped, hidden libraries mishandled; bookkeeping over cloned repositories.
SecretsManager list_secrets filters return nothing; secret-store semantics, but an AWS mock rather than git.
checkout with force=True still prompts before deleting; destructive-operation semantics, which a purge also has to get right.
NameError in the zip-unpacking path; only the fetch-a-project-from-somewhere theme connects it.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: iterobjects_subset raises KeyError walking the object store of a real repo - debugging object enumeration, the core of finding unreachable blobs.
reset_index leaves stale entries because build_index_from_tree misbehaves; index-versus-tree reasoning in a pure-Python git.
porcelain.add corrupts the branch ref; a git write path that silently damages repository state.
Branch sections in .git/config with brackets are parsed wrongly; the ref/config layer this task must not disturb.
describe fails on tagless repositories; walking history to name a commit, a git-internals API fix.
Annotated tag creation fails; constructing a tag object correctly is object-format work.
index.diff silently returns nothing when diff.external is configured - a git query that lies about the repository's contents.
Config parsing of local clone paths with trailing backslashes; config-file edge cases in a git implementation.
Path-to-repository-relative conversion fails at a filesystem root; small validation fix inside a git wrapper.
Rejects fully-qualified refs/heads names; ref-naming discipline, which matters when a rewrite touches refs.

Terminal-Lego-15k.reason: Remove a sensitive file from git history - the exact cleanup half, including making it unrecoverable rather than just deleted.
Script the recovery of a dropped stash by finding the lost commit in the object store - the same unreachable-object hunt.
Shrink .git by purging historical blobs: rewrite, expire reflogs, gc --prune. Exactly what makes a secret truly gone.
Repair an empty/corrupt loose object; forces working directly on .git/objects rather than through porcelain.
Diagnose a repository that clients refuse to open; inspecting refs and object integrity to find what is structurally wrong.
Move HEAD back and undo commits via detached HEAD; understanding that reset does not destroy the commits it leaves behind.
Delete a stash made with git stash create, which exists only as an unreferenced commit - deleting an object nothing points at.
Extract one file out of a stash without popping it; reading content out of a commit you are not checking out.
Undo a git pull using ORIG_HEAD; recovering a prior state from a reference git kept for you.
Revert the initial commit, the one case needing a rewrite rather than a revert; strong verifier, narrow skill.

CalibForge.reason: Recover every secret from a repo whose history was cleaned, then verify nothing remains recoverable - both halves of this task, strong verifier.
Recover a formatted secret key still reachable in history and write it to /app/secret.txt; same premise, same deliverable path.
Recover the true history then rewrite it so a file was never tracked, leaving fsck clean and tags intact - the purge half, strongly verified.
A force-push removed sensitive files but the object database still holds them as unreachable objects; recover them.
Audit a repo after a panicked cleanup of new commits, deleted branches and force-pushes; find ALL secrets, not just the obvious one.
Attacker deleted files to hide tracks; mine the object database for unreferenced data - same reasoning, incident-response framing.
Recover a database password from a history the developer tried to clean; short, direct, same recovery skill.
Write a scanner that sweeps every commit for credentials; generalises the search step and is strongly verified.
Scrambled object files hide secret.txt's contents; recover them by reading the object store directly rather than via git.
Recovered workstation backup with a repo containing committed sensitive configuration; forensics with more environment setup than digging.

final_top10.reason: Recover every secret from a cleaned history and verify none remains recoverable; both halves of this task, strong verifier.
Recover a formatted secret key from a history the developer tried to purge and write it to /app/secret.txt - same premise and same path.
Remove a sensitive file from git history so it is genuinely unrecoverable; the cleanup requirement this task grades separately.
Recover history, then rewrite it so a file was never tracked, leaving fsck clean and everything else intact - strongest verifier of the group.
Locate the dangling commit that added secret.key in a bare repo and show it; the unreachable-object hunt, though verifier-absent.
Files removed by a force-push survive as unreachable objects; recover them from the object database.
Search git history for an API key committed then removed; the recovery half with a strong verifier.
Recover a dropped stash by finding the commit nothing references any more - same fsck/dangling-object technique.
Expunge the commit that added secret.key from a remote's history; the purge step, graded rather than FREE.
Full audit after a panicked cleanup: find ALL exposed secrets, not just the first one - matches the find-every-occurrence requirement.

notes: This is the best-covered of my five tasks: five of the seven corpora field genuinely close candidates, and the final ten are split across four of them rather than dominated by one. CalibForge has an entire committed-a-secret-then-cleaned-up family, several of them graded strong or ok, and it is the only corpus that also covers the verify-nothing-remains half. Terminal-Lego contributes the two best single-skill tasks (remove-a-file-from-history, recover-a-dropped-stash) plus a deep bench of git-internals exercises - it clearly beats the old pool here. SWE-Rebench is unusually useful for once because dulwich is a from-scratch Git implementation: those entries teach the object store even though their task_form is wrong. SWE-Smith is the only genuinely weak corpus for this task - no Git-internals repo exists in it, and ranks 8-10 are filler. Caution for the merge: several of the closest matches anywhere in the pool (tw_6480, security_20260606_153537_001, security_20260419_182351_003, security_20260509_154924_007) are FREE, and FREE is particularly toxic here because writing a plausible secret[...] string into a file satisfies a substring check without touching the repository.
